content.rendered:
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. Your feet. Not just the feet of the apostles. Not just the feet of angels. Your feet. Every believer in Christ shares in the victory the King is bringing to complete conclusion.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, July 26, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.”
Romans 16:20 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul is closing the letter to the Romans. He has already walked the church through the deepest theological argument in the entire New Testament. Justification by faith. Life in the Spirit. The security of the believer in Christ. He has named individuals to greet in the closing chapter. And then, almost as an aside dropped into the farewell paragraph, he plants one of the most staggering sentences in the whole letter. The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.

The image is deliberately drawn from Genesis 3:15, the first prophecy of the whole Bible. In the garden of Eden, immediately after the fall, God speaks to the serpent and promises that the seed of the woman will crush his head. That prophecy travelled through the entire Old Testament, through the incarnation, through the cross, through the resurrection, through Pentecost, through the spread of the church, and finally, in Romans 16, arrives at the ordinary Roman believer’s feet. The God who promised the serpent’s head would be crushed is doing the crushing through the church.

The pronoun matters. Under your feet. Paul is not saying under the feet of the apostles alone. Not under the feet of the professional clergy alone. Not under the feet of a distant heavenly army. Under your feet. The Roman believers reading Paul’s letter, the tent makers and the household slaves and the widows and the merchants and the day labourers, are the ones through whom the ancient promise of Genesis 3:15 is being fulfilled. And the same is true today. The believer walking to work on Monday morning, the mother preparing school lunches, the pastor writing a Sunday sermon, the tech worker at their laptop, the farmer on the land, is a foot through which God is crushing the ancient enemy.

This is where the two-week series on the believer’s authority arrives. Not at a triumphalist strut. At the quiet certainty of a settled outcome. The war is not yours to win. The war has been won at the cross. The clean-up operation, if we can call it that, is what the church is walking through in every generation until the King returns. Every prayer offered in Jesus’ name, every stronghold demolished by the weapons of the Spirit, every accusation answered by the blood of the Lamb, every deliverance, every healing, every act of gospel witness, is a piece of the serpent’s head being pressed under the feet of the church by the God of peace Himself.

Paul closes the sentence with something extraordinary. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you. That is the fuel of the whole thing. The believer walks in authority not as a triumphalist self-declaration but under the constant grace of Jesus. The grace that saved you. The grace that sustains you. The grace that will finish the work.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the two-week series ends here. You have been given authority. All authority in heaven and on earth belongs to Jesus. He holds the keys of the kingdom. His name is above every name. Greater works are ours. The resurrection power raised Him and lives in you. The weapons of your warfare demolish strongholds. The One in you is greater than the one in the world. Resist and the enemy will flee. The full armor is yours. The powers have been disarmed at the cross. Signs will follow those who believe. The blood of the Lamb has overcome the accuser. And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. Walk in every one of these truths. They belong to you in Christ. And His grace is with you today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You, the God of peace, will soon crush Satan under my feet. Not somewhere else. Under my feet. The ancient promise of Genesis 3:15 is being fulfilled through the church, and I am part of that church. Every prayer, every act of obedience, every step of faith today is part of Your finishing work. I walk in the authority You have given me. I stand on the ground Jesus has already secured. I live under the constant grace of the Lord Jesus. And I trust You to complete what You have started. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The God of peace will soon crush Satan under my feet. The ancient promise is being fulfilled through the church. The grace of the Lord Jesus is with me. I walk in it today.
